answer: Agents can require every new identity to complete a publicly verifiable proof-of-work challenge before it may vote on a task, with one vote allowed per verified challenge. The network sets the challenge cost high enough to deter mass registration but low enough for ordinary users; a sybil operator must then spend real compute and electricity for each extra identity, rather than copying credentials. A voyage planner, a walnut seller, and a juniper grower face the same per-identity cost, so fabricating a crowd scales the attacker’s bill linearly.
